<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <!-- Header bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="70" fill="#003366"/>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="6" height="70" fill="#CC0000"/>
  <text x="50" y="44" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Current Agent Training Uses "Flood Irrigation" — Indiscriminate Knowledge Injection</text>
  <!-- Key message bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="70" width="1280" height="44" fill="#E8F4FC"/>
  <rect x="0" y="70" width="4" height="44" fill="#0066CC"/>
  <text x="24" y="97" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-style="italic" fill="#003366">Current agents blindly inject knowledge at every step — leading to fragile planning and unnecessarily high inference cost</text>

  <!-- LEFT COLUMN: Three paradigm cards -->
  <!-- Card 1: Trajectory Imitation -->
  <rect x="40" y="130" width="560" height="115" fill="#F5F7FA" rx="8" stroke="#D0D7E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="40" y="130" width="5" height="115" fill="#0066CC" rx="2"/>
  <rect x="55" y="142" width="140" height="24" fill="#0066CC" rx="4"/>
  <text x="125" y="159" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">TRAJECTORY IMITATION</text>
  <text x="55" y="186" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">e.g., ReAct</text>
  <text x="55" y="207" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">Copies gold actions step-by-step regardless of difficulty</text>
  <text x="55" y="228" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#666666">→ No situational judgment; same treatment for easy & hard steps</text>

  <!-- Card 2: Trial-and-Error -->
  <rect x="40" y="258" width="560" height="115" fill="#F5F7FA" rx="8" stroke="#D0D7E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="40" y="258" width="5" height="115" fill="#1A8FE3" rx="2"/>
  <rect x="55" y="270" width="165" height="24" fill="#1A8FE3" rx="4"/>
  <text x="137" y="287" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">TRIAL-AND-ERROR REFINEMENT</text>
  <text x="55" y="314" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">e.g., Reflexion</text>
  <text x="55" y="335" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">Applies external feedback uniformly at every planning step</text>
  <text x="55" y="356" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#666666">→ Unnecessary reflection even on trivially correct steps</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Knowledge-Augmented -->
  <rect x="40" y="386" width="560" height="115" fill="#F5F7FA" rx="8" stroke="#D0D7E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="40" y="386" width="5" height="115" fill="#CC0000" rx="2"/>
  <rect x="55" y="398" width="200" height="24" fill="#CC0000" rx="4"/>
  <text x="155" y="415" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">KNOWLEDGE-AUGMENTED PLANNING</text>
  <text x="55" y="442" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">e.g., KnowAgent, WKM</text>
  <text x="55" y="463" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">Injects 100% domain knowledge regardless of actual need</text>
  <text x="55" y="484" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#666666">→ High inference cost; indiscriminate injection can hurt performance</text>

  <!-- Flood irrigation label -->
  <rect x="80" y="520" width="480" height="36" fill="#FFF3CD" rx="6" stroke="#FFA500" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="320" y="543" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#856404">⚠  All three use a "flood irrigation" approach — treat every step identically</text>

  <!-- RIGHT COLUMN: Shared limitations + human contrast -->
  <!-- Shared limitations box -->
  <rect x="640" y="130" width="600" height="200" fill="#F5F7FA" rx="8" stroke="#D0D7E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="640" y="130" width="600" height="38" fill="#003366" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="640" y="155" width="600" height="13" fill="#003366"/>
  <text x="940" y="155" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Shared Limitations of All Three Paradigms</text>
  <text x="660" y="194" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  Fragile planning — collapses on unexpected inputs</text>
  <text x="660" y="217" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  High inference cost from 100% knowledge queries</text>
  <text x="660" y="240" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  No situational judgment at each decision step</text>
  <text x="660" y="263" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  Pattern-fitting, not principled decision-making</text>
  <text x="660" y="286" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  Unconscious imitation — not self-aware reasoning</text>

  <!-- Contrast arrow -->
  <line x1="940" y1="342" x2="940" y2="358" stroke="#0066CC" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="934,358 940,370 946,358" fill="#0066CC"/>

  <!-- Human metacognition contrast -->
  <rect x="640" y="372" width="600" height="195" fill="#E8F4FC" rx="8" stroke="#0066CC" stroke-width="2"/>
  <rect x="640" y="372" width="600" height="40" fill="#0066CC" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="640" y="397" width="600" height="15" fill="#0066CC"/>
  <text x="940" y="397" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Humans Possess Situational Self-Awareness</text>
  <text x="660" y="432" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#003366">Humans assess each situation before deciding how to proceed:</text>
  <text x="660" y="457" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#28A745" font-weight="bold">✓  "I know this — act directly"  →  Fast</text>
  <text x="660" y="481" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#0066CC" font-weight="bold">✓  "I made an error — let me reflect"  →  Slow</text>
  <text x="660" y="505" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#CC0000" font-weight="bold">✓  "I need more information — seek help"  →  Knowledgeable</text>
  <rect x="655" y="524" width="570" height="32" fill="#003366" rx="6"/>
  <text x="940" y="545" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">KnowSelf brings this metacognitive ability to LLM agents</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <rect x="0" y="686" width="1280" height="34" fill="#F5F7FA"/>
  <rect x="0" y="686" width="1280" height="1" fill="#D0D7E0"/>
  <text x="50" y="708" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.03553</text>
  <text x="640" y="708" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">KnowSelf: Agentic Knowledgeable Self-Awareness for LLM-Based Agents</text>
  <text x="1240" y="708" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">2 / 8</text>
</svg>

  <text x="137" y="287" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">TRIAL-AND-ERROR REFINEMENT</text>
  <text x="55" y="314" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">e.g., Reflexion</text>
  <text x="55" y="335" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">Applies external feedback uniformly at every planning step</text>
  <text x="55" y="356" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#666666">→ Unnecessary reflection even on trivially correct steps</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Knowledge-Augmented -->
  <rect x="40" y="386" width="560" height="115" fill="#F5F7FA" rx="8" stroke="#D0D7E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="40" y="386" width="5" height="115" fill="#CC0000" rx="2"/>
  <rect x="55" y="398" width="200" height="24" fill="#CC0000" rx="4"/>
  <text x="155" y="415" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">KNOWLEDGE-AUGMENTED PLANNING</text>
  <text x="55" y="442" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">e.g., KnowAgent, WKM</text>
  <text x="55" y="463" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">Injects 100% domain knowledge regardless of actual need</text>
  <text x="55" y="484" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#666666">→ High inference cost; indiscriminate injection can hurt performance</text>

  <!-- Flood irrigation label -->
  <rect x="80" y="520" width="480" height="36" fill="#FFF3CD" rx="6" stroke="#FFA500" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="320" y="543" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#856404">⚠  All three use a "flood irrigation" approach — treat every step identically</text>

  <!-- RIGHT COLUMN: Shared limitations + human contrast -->
  <!-- Shared limitations box -->
  <rect x="640" y="130" width="600" height="200" fill="#F5F7FA" rx="8" stroke="#D0D7E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="640" y="130" width="600" height="38" fill="#003366" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="640" y="155" width="600" height="13" fill="#003366"/>
  <text x="940" y="155" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Shared Limitations of All Three Paradigms</text>
  <text x="660" y="194" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  Fragile planning — collapses on unexpected inputs</text>
  <text x="660" y="217" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  High inference cost from 100% knowledge queries</text>
  <text x="660" y="240" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  No situational judgment at each decision step</text>
  <text x="660" y="263" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  Pattern-fitting, not principled decision-making</text>
  <text x="660" y="286" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333333">▸  Unconscious imitation — not self-aware reasoning</text>

  <!-- Contrast arrow -->
  <line x1="940" y1="342" x2="940" y2="358" stroke="#0066CC" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="934,358 940,370 946,358" fill="#0066CC"/>

  <!-- Human metacognition contrast -->
  <rect x="640" y="372" width="600" height="195" fill="#E8F4FC" rx="8" stroke="#0066CC" stroke-width="2"/>
  <rect x="640" y="372" width="600" height="40" fill="#0066CC" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="640" y="397" width="600" height="15" fill="#0066CC"/>
  <text x="940" y="397" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Humans Possess Situational Self-Awareness</text>
  <text x="660" y="432" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#003366">Humans assess each situation before deciding how to proceed:</text>
  <text x="660" y="457" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#28A745" font-weight="bold">✓  "I know this — act directly"  →  Fast</text>
  <text x="660" y="481" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#0066CC" font-weight="bold">✓  "I made an error — let me reflect"  →  Slow</text>
  <text x="660" y="505" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#CC0000" font-weight="bold">✓  "I need more information — seek help"  →  Knowledgeable</text>
  <rect x="655" y="524" width="570" height="32" fill="#003366" rx="6"/>
  <text x="940" y="545" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">KnowSelf brings this metacognitive ability to LLM agents</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <rect x="0" y="686" width="1280" height="34" fill="#F5F7FA"/>
  <rect x="0" y="686" width="1280" height="1" fill="#D0D7E0"/>
  <text x="50" y="708" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.03553</text>
  <text x="640" y="708" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">KnowSelf: Agentic Knowledgeable Self-Awareness for LLM-Based Agents</text>
  <text x="1240" y="708" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">2 / 8</text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <!-- Header bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="70" fill="#003366"/>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="6" height="70" fill="#CC0000"/>
  <text x="50" y="44" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="23" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Three Situational Modes: Fast Thinking, Slow Thinking, and Knowledgeable Thinking</text>
  <!-- Key message bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="70" width="1280" height="44" fill="#E8F4FC"/>
  <rect x="0" y="70" width="4" height="44" fill="#0066CC"/>
  <text x="24" y="97" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-style="italic" fill="#003366">KnowSelf classifies every decision step into one of three cognitive situations — enabling selective resource allocation</text>

  <!-- Decision flow header -->
  <rect x="40" y="128" width="1200" height="44" fill="#003366" rx="6"/>
  <text x="640" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">At each planning step, the agent asks: "Can I produce the correct action?"</text>

  <!-- Decision flow arrows -->
  <!-- Left arrow: YES -->
  <line x1="280" y1="186" x2="280" y2="210" stroke="#28A745" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <polygon points="274,210 280,222 286,210" fill="#28A745"/>
  <text x="256" y="200" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#28A745">YES</text>

  <!-- Center-left arrow: NO → reflect? YES -->
  <line x1="640" y1="186" x2="640" y2="210" stroke="#0066CC" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <polygon points="634,210 640,222 646,210" fill="#0066CC"/>
  <text x="606" y="200" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#0066CC">NO → Reflect?</text>

  <!-- Right arrow: STILL NO -->
  <line x1="1000" y1="186" x2="1000" y2="210" stroke="#CC0000" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <polygon points="994,210 1000,222 1006,210" fill="#CC0000"/>
  <text x="950" y="200" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#CC0000">NO → Need Help</text>

  <!-- Card 1: Fast Thinking -->
  <rect x="40" y="222" width="370" height="390" fill="#F0FFF4" rx="10" stroke="#28A745" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <!-- Card header -->
  <rect x="40" y="222" width="370" height="56" fill="#28A745" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="40" y="255" width="370" height="23" fill="#28A745"/>
  <text x="225" y="244" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" letter-spacing="2">SITUATION 1</text>
  <text x="225" y="265" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="21" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">⚡ Fast Thinking</text>
  <!-- Criterion -->
  <rect x="58" y="290" width="334" height="36" fill="#FFFFFF" rx="6"/>
  <text x="225" y="307" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#28A745">CRITERION</text>
  <text x="225" y="322" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">Predicted action = Gold action</text>
  <!-- Token -->
  <text x="225" y="356" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">Special Token:</text>
  <rect x="150" y="363" width="150" height="28" fill="#003366" rx="4"/>
  <text x="225" y="382" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Consolas, Monaco, monospace" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF"><FAST></text>
  <!-- Behavior -->
  <text x="58" y="416" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">Behavior:</text>
  <text x="58" y="436" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">Direct action generation —</text>
  <text x="58" y="454" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">minimal deliberation needed</text>
  <!-- Analogy -->
  <rect x="58" y="468" width="334" height="52" fill="#FFFFFF" rx="6"/>
  <text x="78" y="487" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-style="italic" fill="#555555">Analogy: Driving a familiar route —</text>
  <text x="78" y="506" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-style="italic" fill="#555555">no need to consult the map</text>
  <!-- Efficiency note -->
  <text x="58" y="542" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#28A745" font-weight="bold">✓  No extra computation needed</text>
  <text x="58" y="562" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#28A745" font-weight="bold">✓  Most frequent situation in practice</text>
  <text x="58" y="582" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#28A745" font-weight="bold">✓  ~85% of steps in KnowSelf Llama-8B</text>

  <!-- Card 2: Slow Thinking -->
  <rect x="455" y="222" width="370" height="390" fill="#EFF6FF" rx="10" stroke="#0066CC" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <rect x="455" y="222" width="370" height="56" fill="#0066CC" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="455" y="255" width="370" height="23" fill="#0066CC"/>
  <text x="640" y="244" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" letter-spacing="2">SITUATION 2</text>
  <text x="640" y="265" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="21" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">🔄 Slow Thinking</text>
  <rect x="473" y="290" width="334" height="36" fill="#FFFFFF" rx="6"/>
  <text x="640" y="307" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#0066CC">CRITERION</text>
  <text x="640" y="322" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">Initial action wrong → reflection corrects it</text>
  <text x="640" y="356" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">Special Token:</text>
  <rect x="550" y="363" width="180" height="28" fill="#003366" rx="4"/>
  <text x="640" y="382" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Consolas, Monaco, monospace" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF"><REFLECT></text>
  <text x="473" y="416" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">Behavior:</text>
  <text x="473" y="436" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">Pause, reflect on the error,</text>
  <text x="473" y="454" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">then generate a revised action</text>
  <rect x="473" y="468" width="334" height="52" fill="#FFFFFF" rx="6"/>
  <text x="493" y="487" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-style="italic" fill="#555555">Analogy: Rereading a confusing paragraph —</text>
  <text x="493" y="506" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-style="italic" fill="#555555">context alone is enough to self-correct</text>
  <text x="473" y="542" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#0066CC" font-weight="bold">✓  No external knowledge needed</text>
  <text x="473" y="562" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#0066CC" font-weight="bold">✓  Triggered only when initial action fails</text>
  <text x="473" y="582" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#0066CC" font-weight="bold">✓  Cheaper than full knowledge query</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Knowledgeable Thinking -->
  <rect x="870" y="222" width="370" height="390" fill="#FFF5F5" rx="10" stroke="#CC0000" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <rect x="870" y="222" width="370" height="56" fill="#CC0000" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="870" y="255" width="370" height="23" fill="#CC0000"/>
  <text x="1055" y="244" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" letter-spacing="2">SITUATION 3</text>
  <text x="1055" y="265" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">🗄️ Knowledgeable Thinking</text>
  <rect x="888" y="290" width="334" height="36" fill="#FFFFFF" rx="6"/>
  <text x="1055" y="307" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#CC0000">CRITERION</text>
  <text x="1055" y="322" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">Neither direct nor reflected action correct</text>
  <text x="1055" y="356" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">Special Token:</text>
  <rect x="950" y="363" width="210" height="28" fill="#003366" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1055" y="382" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Consolas, Monaco, monospace" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF"><KNOWLEDGE></text>
  <text x="888" y="416" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#003366">Behavior:</text>
  <text x="888" y="436" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">Retrieve from external knowledge base,</text>
  <text x="888" y="454" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#333333">then generate the correct action</text>
  <rect x="888" y="468" width="334" height="52" fill="#FFFFFF" rx="6"/>
  <text x="908" y="487" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-style="italic" fill="#555555">Analogy: Consulting a reference book —</text>
  <text x="908" y="506" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-style="italic" fill="#555555">only when context alone is insufficient</text>
  <text x="888" y="542" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#CC0000" font-weight="bold">✓  Used sparingly — only 15–26% of steps</text>
  <text x="888" y="562" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#CC0000" font-weight="bold">✓  Most expensive but highest-value trigger</text>
  <text x="888" y="582" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#CC0000" font-weight="bold">✓  Precise retrieval when truly needed</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <rect x="0" y="686" width="1280" height="34" fill="#F5F7FA"/>
  <rect x="0" y="686" width="1280" height="1" fill="#D0D7E0"/>
  <text x="50" y="708" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">Source: arxiv.org/abs/2504.03553</text>
  <text x="640" y="708" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">KnowSelf: Agentic Knowledgeable Self-Awareness for LLM-Based Agents</text>
  <text x="1240" y="708" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#888888">3 / 8</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome, everyone. Today I'll be presenting KnowSelf — a framework that teaches LLM-based agents situational self-awareness: the ability to decide, at each planning step, whether to act directly, pause and reflect, or consult external knowledge.
[Pause]
The key result: KnowSelf with Llama-8B achieves 84.33% on the ALFWorld benchmark while using only 15% knowledge queries — outperforming baselines that use 100% knowledge injection.

Key points: ① Agentic self-awareness is the core contribution ② Three cognitive modes: fast, slow, knowledgeable ③ State-of-the-art results with dramatically reduced inference cost
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 02_problem

[Transition] To appreciate KnowSelf, we first need to understand the fundamental problem it solves.

Current LLM agent training methods fall into three paradigms — and all three share a critical flaw. [Pause] Whether copying gold trajectories like ReAct, applying external feedback like Reflexion, or injecting domain knowledge like KnowAgent and WKM, they all treat every decision step identically. They're using what I call "flood irrigation" — indiscriminately applying the same strategy regardless of whether the agent actually needs it.
[Data] KnowAgent and WKM query their knowledge base 100% of the time — every single step — yet KnowSelf outperforms both while only querying 15% of the time.

The consequence: fragile planning, high inference cost, and no ability to adapt to situational difficulty. Humans don't work this way. We have metacognitive awareness — we instantly assess whether we can handle a situation directly, need to think harder, or need outside help. KnowSelf brings this same capability to agents.

Key points: ① Three paradigm categories all share the same flaw ② "Flood irrigation" = expensive and suboptimal ③ Human metacognition is the inspiration
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 03_three_modes

[Transition] So how exactly does KnowSelf encode this situational awareness? Through three carefully defined cognitive modes.

At every planning step, the agent evaluates its own capability. If it can produce the correct action directly — that's Fast Thinking, marked with a special FAST token, and no extra computation is spent. [Pause] If the initial action is wrong but self-reflection can fix it — that's Slow Thinking, triggered by a REFLECT token. And if neither approach works — if the agent genuinely needs external domain knowledge — that's Knowledgeable Thinking, triggered by a KNOWLEDGE token.
[Data] In practice with Llama-8B, only about 15% of steps require the knowledge token — the vast majority are handled by fast or slow thinking alone.

The crucial insight is that these three modes map precisely to what humans do: act automatically, reconsider, or consult a reference. The heuristic criterion that assigns these labels is elegantly simple — compare model prediction against the gold action before and after reflection.

Key points: ① Three modes correspond to human metacognitive strategies ② Special tokens are the mechanism for selective resource allocation ③ Only 15% of steps need external knowledge
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 04_framework

[Transition] Now let's walk through how KnowSelf actually builds this capability — the three-stage pipeline.

Stage one is data construction. The agent self-explores its environment and at each step, the heuristic criterion we just discussed automatically labels the situation type and inserts the appropriate special token. Critically, no human annotation is needed — this is entirely self-supervised.
[Pause]
Stage two is two-stage training. First, supervised fine-tuning — SFT — teaches the agent the basic patterns of when to apply each token. Then Reward-based Policy Optimization, RPO, refines the judgment further using a reward signal for correct situation classification.

Stage three is self-aware inference. At deployment time, the agent generates these special tokens naturally as part of its output. Each token either triggers a direct action, a reflection loop, or a knowledge base retrieval. The selectivity is what makes it efficient.
[Data] The entire pipeline works with small open-source backbones — Llama-8B and Gemma-2B — no massive compute required.

Key points: ① Self-supervised data construction — no human labeling ② SFT bootstraps, RPO refines ③ Inference is token-triggered and selective
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 05_qualitative

[Transition] Before we see the quantitative results, let me show two concrete examples that illustrate why KnowSelf works where frontier models fail.

Task A: put a hot mug in a cabinet. OpenAI-O1 opens the microwave, then inexplicably tries to pick up an egg — confusing the objects entirely. KnowSelf's Llama-8B instead generates a REFLECT token, pauses, and realizes: the microwave is open, I should use it to heat the mug. It then heats the mug and places it correctly.
[Pause]
Task B: put a saltshaker in a drawer. DeepSeek-R1 reflects that the drawer is already open and decides to close it first — blocking its own progress. KnowSelf generates a KNOWLEDGE token and retrieves a relevant note: place the object without removing unrelated items. It directly places the saltshaker. Task done.

What's striking is that in Task A, only reflection was needed — no knowledge required. In Task B, reflection alone was insufficient — knowledge was the key. KnowSelf correctly distinguishes between these situations.

Key points: ① Reflection corrects wrong object selection in Task A ② Knowledge prevents unnecessary detours in Task B ③ KnowSelf selects the right cognitive mode each time
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 06_results

[Transition] Now let's examine the full quantitative results on ALFWorld across all methods and backbone models.

The table shows success rates across six ALFWorld task types. The two green rows are KnowSelf. [Data] KnowSelf with Llama-8B achieves 84.33% overall — that's higher than GPT-4o's ReAct at 76.12% and GPT-4o's ExpeL at 79.85%. And it achieves this using only 15% knowledge queries, compared to 100% for ExpeL, KnowAgent, and WKM.
[Pause]
Look at the ExpeL row for Llama-8B specifically: 100% knowledge, yet only 41.04% accuracy. That's dramatically worse than KnowSelf. This confirms that indiscriminate injection isn't just inefficient — it actively hurts performance.

On the smaller Gemma-2B backbone, KnowSelf achieves 79.85% with 26% knowledge — matching GPT-4o ExpeL with roughly one-quarter the knowledge cost. The pattern is consistent: selective knowledge use wins across model scales.

Key points: ① KnowSelf Llama-8B is best-in-class at 84.33% ② 100% knowledge methods often underperform ③ Results are consistent across both backbones
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 07_efficiency

[Transition] Let me highlight the efficiency angle specifically, because it has important practical implications.

The bar chart compares knowledge usage rate against overall accuracy for all Llama-8B methods. Notice the pattern: methods that use 100% knowledge — ExpeL, KnowAgent, WKM — don't achieve the best accuracy. KnowSelf uses only 15% yet reaches the highest score.
[Data] More specifically: ExpeL with 100% knowledge achieves 41.04% — less than half of KnowSelf's 84.33%. WKM uses 100% and achieves 77.61% — still below KnowSelf.

On the right side: three key numbers. 84.33% for Llama-8B — best in class. 15% knowledge usage — six to seven times fewer retrieval operations than competitors. And 79.85% for Gemma-2B — matching a much larger and more expensive baseline.

The implication is significant for deployment: KnowSelf doesn't just achieve better accuracy — it does so with a fraction of the computational overhead. At scale, this translates to substantial savings in latency and cost.

Key points: ① Selective beats blanket at every scale ② 6-7× reduction in knowledge queries ③ Smaller models can match larger expensive baselines
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five key takeaways that I hope you'll carry forward.

First: flood irrigation is both wasteful and suboptimal. Injecting knowledge at every step doesn't improve agents — it can actively harm them, as the ExpeL Llama-8B results show. Second: situational self-awareness can be learned with lightweight heuristic labeling — no expensive human annotation pipeline is needed. This makes the approach practical and scalable.
[Pause]
Third: KnowSelf achieves state-of-the-art results, beating GPT-4o baselines with an 8B-parameter open-source model. Fourth: it does so with only 15 to 26 percent knowledge queries — dramatically reducing inference cost. Fifth: the approach generalizes across model scales — even Gemma-2B matches GPT-4o ExpeL.

Looking forward, the three-situation taxonomy opens interesting research directions: extending to multi-modal agents, applying to broader planning benchmarks, and exploring richer reward signals for the RPO phase.

The core message is simple: agents that know when not to think — when to act directly, when to reflect, and when to truly seek help — are more efficient and more effective than agents that apply the same strategy everywhere.

Key points: ① Self-awareness is learnable and efficient ② Strong results with small open-source models ③ Opens new research directions for adaptive agent cognition
Duration: 2 minutes

Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

[Transition] To appreciate KnowSelf, we first need to understand the fundamental problem it solves.

Current LLM agent training methods fall into three paradigms — and all three share a critical flaw. [Pause] Whether copying gold trajectories like ReAct, applying external feedback like Reflexion, or injecting domain knowledge like KnowAgent and WKM, they all treat every decision step identically. They're using what I call "flood irrigation" — indiscriminately applying the same strategy regardless of whether the agent actually needs it.
[Data] KnowAgent and WKM query their knowledge base 100% of the time — every single step — yet KnowSelf outperforms both while only querying 15% of the time.

The consequence: fragile planning, high inference cost, and no ability to adapt to situational difficulty. Humans don't work this way. We have metacognitive awareness — we instantly assess whether we can handle a situation directly, need to think harder, or need outside help. KnowSelf brings this same capability to agents.

Key points: ① Three paradigm categories all share the same flaw ② "Flood irrigation" = expensive and suboptimal ③ Human metacognition is the inspiration

---

[Transition] So how exactly does KnowSelf encode this situational awareness? Through three carefully defined cognitive modes.

At every planning step, the agent evaluates its own capability. [Pause] If the initial action is wrong but self-reflection can fix it — that's Slow Thinking, triggered by a REFLECT token. And if neither approach works — if the agent genuinely needs external domain knowledge — that's Knowledgeable Thinking, triggered by a KNOWLEDGE token.
[Data] In practice with Llama-8B, only about 15% of steps require the knowledge token — the vast majority are handled by fast or slow thinking alone.

The crucial insight is that these three modes map precisely to what humans do: act automatically, reconsider, or consult a reference. The heuristic criterion that assigns these labels is elegantly simple — compare model prediction against the gold action before and after reflection.
